steps.name: prompt
steps.text: Write the introduction for our paper on click-based interactive image segmentation (CFR-ICL). It should motivate interactive segmentation, briefly review interaction types and earlier click-based methods, point out what existing losses and refinement schemes lack, introduce our three proposals (iterative click loss, cascade-forward refinement, and the SUEM copy-paste augmentation), and end with a contributions list.

steps.name: skeleton_outline
steps.text:
- Motivation: interactive segmentation and the cost of annotated data
- Interaction types; click-based methods from image processing to deep learning
- Gaps: losses ignore number of clicks; refinement needs extra modules
- Our proposals: ICL, CFR, SUEM Copy-Paste
- Contributions list

steps.name: detailed_outline
steps.text:
- Motivation
  - interactive segmentation = extract object(s) of interest from images with user input
  - essential for broader real-world use of deep learning solutions
  - DNNs need extensive annotated data; expensive, time-consuming (labor costs)
  - interactive segmentation = more cost-effective way to build large-scale labeled datasets
- Interaction types / click-based methods
  - scribbles, boxes, clicks (cite each)
  - this work: clicks; positive = foreground, negative = background
  - earlier click methods: image processing, e.g. connectedness-based approach (cite)
  - then deep learning-based methods, beginning with one early work (cite) -> big performance gains
  - recent DL methods (cite group) -> further efficiency gains
- Gaps
  - many methods (cite group): loss = difference between predicted masks and ground truth; no explicit way to optimize number of clicks
  - some studies (cite): refine initial predictions
  - needs additional trainable modules to identify and fine-grind local areas -> harder training
- Proposals
  - Iterative Click Loss (ICL): penalizes instances with many clicks
  - Cascade-Forward Refinement (CFR): refinement at inference time, improves details, no additional network
  - SUEM Copy-Paste (C&P): augmentation, extension of Simple Copy-Paste (cite), designed for interactive segmentation
- Contributions
  - ICL: first loss encoding number of clicks (to our knowledge); preference for models needing fewer clicks
  - CFR: simple unified framework; applicable to other iterative mask-guided models
  - SUEM: set of four copy-paste approaches; more diversity, bigger training sets in practical settings

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
Interactive image segmentation is about getting the object or objects of interest out of an image with input from a user. It is important for using deep learning-based solutions more broadly in real-world scenarios. Deep neural networks (DNNs) usually need a lot of annotated data, and making that data can be very expensive and takes a lot of time because labor costs are high. Interactive segmentation is a cheaper way to generate large-scale labeled datasets.

There are different kinds of interactions in interactive segmentation, for example scribbles, boxes and clicks. In this work we focus on clicks. In the click-based approach the user gives positive clicks and negative clicks on the image, and these mark the foreground and the background regions. The earlier click-based methods used image processing techniques, for example a connectedness-based approach. Later the field moved to deep learning-based methods, starting with one early work, and these gave big improvements in segmentation performance. More deep learning-based methods have come out recently and they made interactive segmentation even more efficient.

- Gaps
  - many methods: loss = difference between predicted masks and ground truth; no explicit way to optimize number of clicks
  - some studies: refine initial predictions; need additional trainable modules to identify and fine-grind local areas -> harder training
- Proposals
  - ICL: penalizes instances with many clicks
  - CFR: refinement at inference time, improves details, no additional network
  - SUEM Copy-Paste (C&P): extension of Simple Copy-Paste, for interactive segmentation
- Contributions
  - ICL: first loss encoding number of clicks; preference for fewer clicks
  - CFR: simple unified framework; applies to other iterative mask-guided models
  - SUEM: four copy-paste approaches; diversity and size of training sets

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
Interactive image segmentation is about getting the object or objects of interest out of an image with input from a user. It is important for using deep learning-based solutions more broadly in real-world scenarios. Deep neural networks (DNNs) usually need a lot of annotated data, and making that data can be very expensive and takes a lot of time because labor costs are high. Interactive segmentation is a cheaper way to generate large-scale labeled datasets.

There are different kinds of interactions in interactive segmentation, for example scribbles, boxes and clicks. In this work we focus on clicks. In the click-based approach the user gives positive clicks and negative clicks on the image, and these mark the foreground and the background regions. The earlier click-based methods used image processing techniques, for example a connectedness-based approach. Later the field moved to deep learning-based methods, starting with one early work, and these gave big improvements in segmentation performance. More deep learning-based methods have come out recently and they made interactive segmentation even more efficient.

Many interactive segmentation methods define their loss functions from the difference between the predicted masks and the ground truths. They do not have any explicit way to optimize how many clicks the user needs. Some studies also refine the initial predictions to get better outputs. But these techniques need extra trainable network modules to find and fine-grind the local areas in the predicted masks, and this makes the training harder. In this paper we propose an Iterative Click Loss (ICL), which penalizes instances that take a large number of clicks. We also present a new refinement strategy for inference time called Cascade-Forward Refinement (CFR). CFR improves the segmentation details during inference and it does not need an additional network. We also present an image augmentation technique, SUEM Copy-Paste (C&P), which is an extension of the Simple Copy-Paste method and is designed specifically for interactive image segmentation tasks. Our contributions are summarized below.

- As far as we know, the Iterative Click Loss is the first loss that encodes the number of clicks to train an interactive segmentation model. It gives a new way to prefer models that need fewer user clicks.

- Cascade-Forward Refinement improves segmentation quality during inference in a simple, unified framework, and it can be applied to other iterative mask-guided interactive segmentation models.

- In SUEM augmentation we propose a set of four copy-paste augmentation approaches, which greatly improve the diversity and increase the size of training sets in practical settings.

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
Interactive image segmentation extracts object(s) of interest from images with user input. It is essential for enabling a broader application of deep learning-based solutions in real-world scenarios. Deep neural networks (DNNs) often require extensive annotated data, which can be extremely expensive and time-consuming to create because of high labor costs. Interactive segmentation offers a more cost-effective way of generating large-scale labeled datasets.

Interactions in interactive segmentation include scribbles [1], boxes [2], and clicks [3]. This work focuses on the click-based approach, in which the user provides positive and negative clicks on the image to identify foreground and background regions, respectively. Earlier click-based methods were built on image processing techniques, such as the connectedness-based approach described in [3]. Subsequent advances in the field, however, led to deep learning-based methods, beginning with [4], which brought significant improvements in segmentation performance. More recently, further deep learning-based methods have been introduced, including [5,6,7,8], which have further improved the efficiency of interactive segmentation.

Many interactive segmentation methods [5,6,8,7,9] define their loss functions based on the difference between the predicted segmentation masks and the ground truths, and have no explicit way to optimize the number of user clicks. Some studies [8] refine the initial predictions to enhance the quality of the outputs. These techniques require additional trainable network modules to identify and fine-grind local areas in the predicted masks, which makes training more difficult. In this paper, we put forward an Iterative Click Loss (ICL) that imposes penalties on instances with a large number of clicks. We also present a novel refinement strategy for inference time, named Cascade-Forward Refinement (CFR), which is designed to improve segmentation details during inference without the need for an additional network. Finally, we present an effective image augmentation technique, SUEM Copy-Paste (C&P), an extension of the Simple Copy-Paste [10] method designed specifically for interactive image segmentation tasks. The contributions of this work are summarized below.

- To the best of our knowledge, the proposed Iterative Click Loss is the first loss that encodes the number of clicks to train a model for interactive segmentation, and it offers a novel way to define a preference for models that need fewer user clicks.

- The proposed Cascade-Forward Refinement enhances segmentation quality during inference in a simple and unified framework, and it can be applied to other iterative mask-guided interactive segmentation models.

- In the proposed SUEM augmentation, we propose a set of four copy-paste augmentation approaches that greatly improve the diversity and increase the size of training sets in practical settings.
